text:
Evidence supports investigating weak ranking despite good training separation. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024; original RecSys 2023)](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec degradation to overconfidence under sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE. This supports a loss/sampling ablation, but does not establish that multi-negative sampled softmax will win on these four categories. A [2024 negative-sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity-bias tradeoffs across random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling.

Hardness should be controlled. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports that introducing hard negatives too early can harm learning; it uses uniform warm-start followed by curriculum mining. Highest-scoring unobserved items may be false negatives; stochastic selection among several high-ranked candidates reduces deterministic selection risk. Practical experiment, inferred from this evidence: compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE/gBCE and sampled softmax with 16–64 uniform negatives, then introduce a small hard-negative fraction after warm-up. Mask known training positives; never inspect held-out labels to filter negatives. Score bounded candidate pools rather than mining the full catalog at every update.

Select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, even when prioritizing Electronics experiments. Larger training margins alone cannot demonstrate generalization. [Krichene and Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse full-catalog model comparisons; success against 99 negatives therefore does not establish full-catalog recommendation quality. Track category HR@10, validation trajectories and GPU seconds, retaining improvements that justify their search cost.
